questions.q: Which earlier chapter of this course is the direct reason Lesson 30's chaos experiment had a hypothesis, a steady state, and abort criteria instead of just breaking something to see what happens?
options: Chapter 6, On-Call and Operational Excellence
Chapter 1, SRE Principles at Enterprise Scale
Chapter 3, Chaos Engineering and Resilience Testing
Chapter 7, Building an SRE Practice and Culture
questions.explain: Chapter 3's chaos engineering discipline -- hypothesis, steady state, and abort criteria -- is exactly what Lesson 30's experiment applied to a real scenario.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the relationship among the four Expert Specialization courses, including this one?
options: Each of the four must be completed before the next one can be started, in a fixed order
They build on the Advanced Specialization stage but not on each other, so they can be taken in any order once that stage is complete
This SRE course must be completed first because the other three depend on it directly
Only one of the four courses is actually required to reach Cloud Architect
questions.explain: The path's own outline states that the four Expert Specialization courses build on the Advanced stage but not on each other, making their order flexible.

questions.q: How many courses make up the Job-Ready Foundation stage of the Cloud Engineer to Cloud Architect path, according to this lesson?
options: Seven
Four
Eleven
Fifteen
questions.explain: Job-Ready Foundation is seven courses, from How IT Teams Work through the Cloud Deployment, Monitoring, Backup & Job-Ready Capstone.

questions.q: What does this path's own destination note say Expert Specialization opens doors toward, beyond Cloud Architect itself?
options: Only Site Reliability Engineer roles, since that is this specific course
Platform Engineer, Multi-Cloud/Enterprise Architect, AI Infrastructure Engineer, or Site Reliability Engineer roles
A return to Cloud Support Engineer roles for further on-the-job training
Exclusively academic or graduate-level research positions
questions.explain: The destination note names four doors Expert Specialization opens, this course's SRE track being one of them alongside Platform Engineer, Multi-Cloud/Enterprise Architect, and AI Infrastructure Engineer.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as the real skill the entire fifteen-course path was building toward?
options: Memorizing every Azure and AWS service name across both clouds
Passing a specific cloud vendor certification exam
Writing Terraform modules exclusively, without ever touching Kubernetes
Asking whether something that looks redundant is actually redundant, all the way down to its shared dependencies
questions.explain: Lesson 31's case study and this closing lesson both point to the same real skill: questioning apparent redundancy at every layer, not just the application layer.
